description: Schema definition used to create the Hall of Fame Entry table (layer 9/9, FINAL layer of the Poutine League Dataverse data model build-out): rpo_HallOfFameEntry. Source of truth: ARCHITECTURE.md Sec 1 (Data model), HALL_OF_FAME_ENTRY entity block: 'All-time winners, archived at season close... Lookup to Season, lookup to Category, winner (employee or poutine), badge/title text.'

designDecision.problem: ARCHITECTURE.md describes the winner as polymorphic ('employee or poutine'), depending on the crowned Category's computation type.
designDecision.chosenApproach: Unlike Season Result (which stores a FULL ranked list and needed a child table, rpo_SeasonResultEntry), Hall of Fame Entry stores exactly ONE winner (top-1) per season+category. Modeled directly on rpo_HallOfFameEntry as two nullable lookups -- rpo_EmployeeId (systemuser) and rpo_PoutineSubmissionId (rpo_PoutineSubmission) -- exactly one populated per row depending on the Category's computationtype. No child table needed; this is simpler than layer 8's decomposition, per the coordinator's design note.

tables.purpose: All-time winner record, archived at season close: one row per season+category combination representing the crowned top-1 winner.

columns.notes: Primary name column, auto-created with the table. Seed data composes '<Season name> - <Category name> Champion'.
Human-readable badge/title text, e.g. 'Season Winter 2025-2026 -- Best Critic Champion'.

lookups.creationMethod: client.tables.create_lookup_field() -- created with default RequiredLevel=None, then patched to ApplicationRequired via raw Web API PUT on the LookupAttributeMetadata resource (matches layer 8's Season lookup requiredness on rpo_SeasonResult).
client.tables.create_lookup_field() -- same RequiredLevel patch as rpo_SeasonId above.

client.tables.create_lookup_field() FAILS for lookups to systemuser (documented gotcha: auto-generated relationship schema name lacks a customization prefix). Worked around by calling client.tables.create_one_to_many_relationship() directly with LookupAttributeMetadata + OneToManyRelationshipMetadata, supplying an explicit rpo_-prefixed relationship schema name ('rpo_HallOfFameEntry_Employee').
lookups.notes: Nullable. Populated only when the crowned Category's computationtype is employee-based (try_count_by_submitter, try_count_by_employee, review_helpfulness_score). Exactly one of rpo_EmployeeId / rpo_PoutineSubmissionId is populated per row -- never both, never neither.

lookups.creationMethod: client.tables.create_lookup_field() -- worked as-is (referenced table already carries the rpo prefix).
lookups.notes: Nullable. Populated only when the crowned Category's computationtype is poutine-based (weighted_rating).

solutionAttachment.verificationMethod: Queried solutioncomponent for componenttype=1 filtered to solutionid=poutineleaguecore and confirmed rpo_halloffameentry (MetadataId a7a23e4b-1c31-45dd-a883-dbffc5eee0b7) is present, attached automatically via the solution= parameter on client.tables.create() (no pac solution add-solution-component call was needed, consistent with layers 4 and 8).

creationMethod.tool: PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client (Python SDK) with raw Web API for the RequiredLevel patch on the two required lookups.
creationMethod.phasedCreation: Table created first (with rpo_BadgeTitle column inline), waited ~45s for metadata propagation, then all 4 lookups created sequentially (Season, Category, PoutineSubmission, Employee) with pauses between each, using a retry_metadata wrapper (per dv-metadata's metadata-propagation.md) to absorb transient 'entity not found in MetadataCache' lock-contention errors on the Category and Employee lookups.
creationMethod.gotchasEncountered: Transient 'EntityId not found in MetadataCache.LazyDynamicMetadataCache' errors recurred on 2-3 of the lookup creations despite 20-45s waits after table creation -- resolved with a retry-with-backoff wrapper (20s, 40s, 60s...) rather than a single fixed wait. This is a slightly worse propagation delay than layer 8 saw, but no delete+recreate cycles were needed.
